checklist.step: Take in the annuity product or disclosure change and open a content workbook
actions: Pull the approved change request from the Insurance Product Manager and record product name, contract form number, group vs individual, fixed / indexed / variable, writing company and NAIC co-code, target first-sale date and the state list.
Open a new disclosure content workbook named <product>-<contract form number>-<target sale date> in the annuity forms folder.

Ask the Insurance Product Manager which distribution channels will sell it (face-to-face agent, telephone, mail, web self-service) because Model 245 Section 4B sets a different delivery point for non-face-to-face sales.
Attach the signed change request and the product specification to the workbook.
checklist.done: the workbook names the product, contract form number, writing company, channels and state list, with the change request attached.

checklist.step: Rebuild the Section 4C content matrix for this contract
actions: Create one workbook row per Model 245 Section 4C required element: generic contract name, company name and address, contract identification number, plain-language description of benefits stressing the long-term nature of the contract, guaranteed / non-guaranteed / determinable elements and their limitations, how interest is credited, periodic income (annuitization) options, surrender and withdrawal charge schedule and charge period, market value adjustment, mortality and expense, contract and administrative fees, rider charges and their impact, the IRC 10% early-distribution tax penalty, and the contact point for questions.
Add rows for the state-driven items: free-look length and refund basis, and the Buyer's Guide delivery statement.
Get the surrender charge schedule, MVA formula and rider charge table from the Product / Filing Actuary in writing and paste the figures onto the rows rather than retyping them.
Mark any element the product genuinely does not have as 'N/A — product has no MVA' with the actuary named, never leave a blank row.
checklist.done: every Section 4C element has a row with either drafted content or a named, sourced N/A.

checklist.step: Map each required element to a physical field on a form or letter
actions: For each content row, name the carrier document that will hold it: disclosure document form number, application page, contract data page, or the issue cover letter.
Record the page and section reference so an examiner can be pointed to the exact place the element appears.
Flag any element that currently has no home — those become new drafting work, not a footnote.
Hand the field list to the Business Systems Analyst so the merge fields that must be populated from the policy admin record are identified early.
checklist.done: each Section 4C element resolves to a named document, page and merge field, with no unhomed elements.

checklist.step: Build the 45-jurisdiction free-look and delivery variation grid
actions: Open the regulatory library entry for Annuity Disclosure (NAIC Model 245) and list the 45 adopting jurisdictions with their adopting statute or regulation cite.

For each state record: free-look days for face-to-face sales, free-look days for mail/telephone/internet sales (Model 245 sets a 15-day floor for non-face-to-face), any enhanced senior free-look, and whether the refund is purchase payments or account value.
Record whether the state requires the disclosure and Buyer's Guide at or before application, or with the contract, for each channel.
Capture the representative jurisdictions to the workbook — Alaska adoption of NAIC Model 245 plus the Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona adoptions — as dated PDFs named <state>-model245-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf.
Send the completed grid to Regulatory Counsel for confirmation before any variable text is drafted.
checklist.done: all 45 jurisdictions have free-look days, refund basis, channel delivery point and a dated source capture.

checklist.step: Fix the correct NAIC Buyer's Guide edition for this product type
actions: Decide the guide from the product type: Buyer's Guide for Deferred Annuities (Fixed), Buyer's Guide for Deferred Annuities (Variable), or the indexed variant, and record the reasoning against the contract's crediting mechanism.
Check each state's adopting text for a state-specific guide or a mandated edition date; several states publish their own annuity buyer's guide instead of the NAIC one.
Download the current NAIC edition, record its edition date and page count, and store it beside the disclosure document in the forms folder.
Add a row to the form inventory linking contract form number to Buyer's Guide edition so the print package cannot pair them wrongly.
checklist.done: the product is locked to a named Buyer's Guide edition per state, stored and linked in the form inventory.

checklist.step: Draft or redline the disclosure document itself
actions: Draft the disclosure document against the Section 4C matrix, keeping the long-term-nature statement and the surrender charge schedule on the first two pages rather than buried.
Set the form number and edition date in the footer of every page in the house format <form prefix>-ANN-DISC (mm/yy).
Bracket the state-variable blocks (free-look days, refund basis, state contact) and list them in a Statement of Variability with the permitted values taken from the variation grid.
Produce a redline against the currently approved edition and summarise, in one paragraph per change, what moved and why.
Circulate the draft to the Product / Filing Actuary to confirm the charge tables and crediting description match the contract.
checklist.done: a footered, bracketed draft exists with a Statement of Variability and an actuary-confirmed charge table.

checklist.step: Draft the delivery acknowledgement form that will prove Section 4B delivery
actions: Draft an acknowledgement capturing: applicant name, contract or application number, the disclosure form number and edition date received, the Buyer's Guide title and edition received, the date received, whether the meeting was face-to-face, and applicant and producer signatures.
Make the date field mandatory and separate from the application signature date so an examiner can test 'at or before application' directly.
Add the non-face-to-face branch that states the free-look days applicable in the applicant's state and the date the free-look starts.
Send the draft to the New Business Case Manager to confirm it can actually be collected in the current application flow and to DocuSign for e-signature tagging.
checklist.done: the acknowledgement captures form numbers, edition dates, a separate receipt date and both signatures, and is e-signature ready.

checklist.step: Build the Section 5 annual report template
actions: Lay out the annual report fields required by Model 245 Section 5: contract value at the beginning and end of the reporting period, total gross purchase payments received, interest credited during the period, surrender value, death benefit, withdrawals and charges deducted during the period.
Add the statement that current values are available on request and the contact channel for that request.
Confirm with the Product / Filing Actuary how each figure is derived so the template maps to policy admin data elements, not to hand calculations.
Set the report period convention (contract anniversary versus calendar year) and record it, because it drives the generation trigger built under REG-011-C03.
checklist.done: the annual report template carries every Section 5 field mapped to a named policy admin data element and a stated period convention.

checklist.step: Run readability, type-size and marketing-consistency checks
actions: Score the disclosure document for Flesch reading ease and record the score and the tool used; re-write any section scoring below the lowest applicable state minimum.
Check the typeface is no smaller than the state minimum (10-point is the common floor, 12-point in several adopting states) on every page including footnotes and charge tables.
Compare the disclosure wording against the sales brochures and the Broker & Agent Portal product page so no marketing piece promises a benefit the disclosure limits.
Log every wording conflict back to the Marketing Manager with a fix date ahead of the target sale date.
checklist.done: a recorded Flesch score, a type-size confirmation per page, and a closed list of marketing-versus-disclosure conflicts.

checklist.step: Check the illustration package against Model 245 Section 6
actions: Confirm whether an annuity illustration will be used in the sale; if yes, apply the Section 6 illustration standards and the Appendix A format.
Verify non-guaranteed elements are shown alongside guaranteed elements on the same page and are not more favourable than the currently declared scale.
Confirm the illustration carries the required identification of the insurer, the producer, the date prepared, and the statement that it is not part of the contract.
Sign the illustration certification and file it with the disclosure workbook.
checklist.done: either a documented 'no illustration used' decision or a certified Appendix A-conforming illustration is on file.

checklist.step: Obtain Regulatory Counsel review of content and every variable block
actions: Read the draft against Model 245 Section 4C element by element using the content matrix as the checklist, initialling each row.

Re-read the free-look and refund text for the 45 adopting jurisdictions against the variation grid and correct any state where the drafted days are shorter than the state minimum or the 15-day non-face-to-face floor.
Confirm the group annuity certificate-holder disclosure obligations are addressed where the certificate holder pays the consideration.
Record confirm-or-overturn in writing on each matrix row and date the sign-off.
checklist.done: every content row and every state variable block carries a dated counsel initial or a written correction.

checklist.step: File the disclosure and acknowledgement forms where the state requires it
actions: For each state, open SERFF Industry menu then Filing Rules, select the state and the annuity TOI/Sub-TOI, and read whether disclosure and acknowledgement forms must be filed, filed for record, or are exempt.
Build the SERFF submission with the form schedule listing each form number and edition date, the Statement of Variability, the readability certification and the cover letter.
Submit and record the SERFF Tracking Number, submission date and disposition date against each form number in the form inventory.
Where a state takes annuity forms outside SERFF, record the alternate portal or paper address and the confirmation reference.
checklist.done: every state shows either a SERFF tracking number with disposition or a cited exemption against each form number.

checklist.step: Publish the edition into the form inventory as the single source of truth
actions: Add one inventory row per form: form number, edition date, product, writing company, states approved, SERFF tracking number, Buyer's Guide edition to pair with, earliest use date and latest use date.
Attach the final PDF, the redline, the Statement of Variability and the counsel sign-off to the row.
Set the record class to the Model 245 retention rule — three years from last use or the conclusion of the next market conduct examination, whichever is later.
Confirm the row is searchable by form number, edition date and state.
checklist.done: the inventory holds one complete, attachment-backed row per form with retention applied and no blank fields.

checklist.step: Release into the correspondence library and retire the superseded edition
actions: Load the approved PDF and the merge-field template into the correspondence library under the new form number and edition date.
Set the superseded edition to inactive with a stop-use date and confirm no print package still references it.
Notify the Policy Admin Ops Lead and the Distribution Operations Manager of the swap date so agent kits and portal downloads change on the same day.
Pull five test prints across three states and confirm the state-variable blocks resolve to the values on the variation grid.
checklist.done: the new edition is live, the old edition is stopped, and five cross-state test prints resolve the variable blocks correctly.

checklist.step: File the content evidence pack for the retention period
actions: Move the content workbook, Section 4C matrix with counsel initials, variation grid with dated state captures, readability score, SERFF confirmations and test prints into the evidence repository under the product and edition date.
Apply the three-years-or-next-examination retention label.
Index the pack by product, form number, edition date and state so a market conduct forms request can be answered without a rebuild.
Record the pack location on the change request and close the change.
checklist.done: a single indexed evidence pack per edition exists with retention applied and its location recorded on the change record.

testing.step: Build the population of annuity disclosure artefacts in use during the period
actions: Extract from the form inventory every disclosure document, Buyer's Guide, acknowledgement form and annual report template with an active use window overlapping the period, by product, form number, edition date and state.
Add the correspondence library's active template list so an edition live in print but absent from the inventory is exposed.
Reconcile the two lists and resolve every difference before sampling; an item in print and not in the inventory is an automatic exception.
testing.done: the population is reconciled between inventory and correspondence library and signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to what the policy admin print stream actually attached
actions: Pull the distinct form numbers and edition dates attached to annuity issue packages during the period from the print history table.
Match each to a population row on form number plus edition date.
List any form number printed that never appeared in the inventory, and any inventory edition never printed, with counts of affected contracts.
Resolve or carry each difference forward as an exception before drawing the sample.
testing.done: every printed form number and edition reconciles to an inventory row or is listed as an exception with a contract count.

testing.step: Draw a reproducible sample across products, editions and states
actions: Take 100% of disclosure editions first used during the period and 100% of editions covering group annuity certificates.
Take 15 further editions selected at random with a recorded seed from the remaining population, and 10 state/edition pairs to test variable text, minimum 30 items overall.
Record the seed, the population size and the draw date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every new edition and every group annuity edition.

testing.step: Re-perform the Section 4C content check element by element
actions: Open the sampled PDF and, without looking at the content matrix, tick each Model 245 Section 4C element off your own list: generic contract name, company name and address, contract identification, long-term-nature statement, guaranteed and non-guaranteed elements with limitations, crediting method, annuitization options, surrender and withdrawal charge schedule and period, market value adjustment, all fees and rider charges, the 10% early-distribution tax penalty, and the questions contact.
Record the page and paragraph where each element appears; 'present somewhere in the pack' is not a pass if it is not in the disclosure document.
Compare your result to the maintained content matrix and treat any difference as an exception, including a present element carrying a stale figure.
Screenshot each missing or defective element into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled edition has an independent element-by-element grid with page references and captured evidence for each gap.

testing.step: Verify the Buyer's Guide edition paired with each sampled disclosure
actions: Read the Buyer's Guide edition linked to the sampled form in the inventory and open the actual PDF held in the correspondence library.
Compare its title and edition date to the NAIC current edition for that product type, and to any state-published guide required by the sampled state.
Confirm the guide is the fixed, indexed or variable version that matches the contract's crediting mechanism.
Any superseded or mismatched guide is an exception with the count of contracts issued on that pairing.
testing.done: every sampled pairing uses the current, product-correct Buyer's Guide, or the mismatch is quantified in contracts.

testing.step: Re-test the state free-look and delivery variable text against the source law
actions: For each sampled state/edition pair, read the state's adopting text (representative: Alaska adoption of NAIC Model 245; also Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona adoptions) as it read on the edition's effective date.
Recompute the free-look days the state requires for face-to-face and for mail/telephone/internet sales and compare to the printed value, applying the Model 245 15-day non-face-to-face floor.
Confirm the refund basis printed (purchase payments versus account value) matches the state requirement and any enhanced senior provision.
A printed period shorter than the state minimum is a reportable breach, not a documentation exception.
testing.done: every sampled state's printed free-look days and refund basis are confirmed against the state text or raised as a breach.

testing.step: Trace filed editions to a SERFF disposition that pre-dates first use
actions: In SERFF Filing Access, search the tracking number recorded against each sampled form number and state.
Confirm the filing covers the same company, form number and edition date and read the disposition and disposition date.
Compare the disposition date to the earliest issue date on which that edition was printed in that state.
Where the inventory claims an exemption instead of a filing, read the cited state instruction and confirm it genuinely exempts annuity disclosure forms.
Capture the SERFF filing detail screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled state/edition traces to a disposed SERFF filing pre-dating first use, or to a verified exemption citation.

testing.step: Recompute the edition changeover and prove superseded editions stopped
actions: For each sampled superseding edition, read its earliest use date and the prior edition's stop-use date from the inventory.
Query the print history for any use of the prior edition after its stop-use date and count the contracts affected.
Confirm the readability score and type-size evidence exist for the superseding edition and are dated before first use.
Any post-stop-date use is quantified in contracts and referred for a re-mail decision.
testing.done: no superseded edition printed after its stop-use date, or the affected contract count is quantified and referred.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying form number, edition date, state, the defective element and the count of contracts issued on it.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: matrix element missed, stale actuarial figure, wrong Buyer's Guide pairing, variable block mis-set, superseded edition left live.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and for any missing Section 4C element or short free-look open a corrected re-mail assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open issue into the next sweep as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a contract count, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the content test
actions: Compute the defect rate by element and compare to the zero-tolerance threshold for missing Section 4C elements and short free-look periods.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored and approved none of the sampled editions, sign the workpaper.
Report results and any re-mail decisions to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, defect rate by element and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Classify the sale channel the moment the application arrives
actions: Open the annuity new business work queue and set the Sale Method field on each case to Face-to-face, Mail, Telephone or Internet from the producer's transmittal and the application signature block.
Where the transmittal is silent, call the producer the same day and record the answer, the producer's National Producer Number and the call date on the case notes.
Set the applicant's state of solicitation, because that state, not the residence state, drives the delivery rule and the free-look days.

Let the channel field drive the workflow branch: face-to-face cases require the acknowledgement before underwriting release, non-face-to-face cases require the pack with the contract plus a free-look notice.
checklist.done: every case carries a sourced Sale Method, a state of solicitation and the correct workflow branch.

checklist.step: Gate face-to-face applications on a dated delivery acknowledgement
actions: Check the imaged application pack for the signed delivery acknowledgement showing the disclosure form number and edition date, the Buyer's Guide title and edition, and the receipt date.
Compare the acknowledgement receipt date to the application signature date — the receipt date must be the same day or earlier under Model 245 Section 4B(1).

Where the acknowledgement is missing or dated after the application, pend the case as a Not In Good Order item, notify the producer through the Broker & Agent Portal the same day, and do not release to issue.
Record the acknowledgement document id and both dates on the notice log row for the case.
checklist.done: no face-to-face case leaves the queue without an acknowledgement dated on or before the application signature date.

checklist.step: Build the non-face-to-face contract delivery pack
actions: Assemble the issue package: contract, data pages, the disclosure document at the edition approved for the state of solicitation, the paired Buyer's Guide edition, and the free-look notice.
Print the free-look notice with the state's own free-look days, never a house default, and never fewer than the 15 days Model 245 requires when the sale was not face-to-face.
State on the notice the date the free-look period starts and the address and phone number for exercising it.
Run the pre-mail package check that every one of those five components resolved, and stop the package if any component is missing rather than mailing a partial pack.
checklist.done: every non-face-to-face pack carries contract, data pages, state-correct disclosure, paired Buyer's Guide and a state-correct free-look notice.

checklist.step: Send the pack through a channel that produces provable delivery
actions: Mail the pack with a tracked service or, where the owner has consented to electronic delivery, send through DocuSign with delivery and open receipts enabled.
Capture the carrier tracking number or the DocuSign envelope id onto the notice log row against the contract number.
Store the exact PDF image that was sent, not the template, in the document repository under the contract number.
Confirm the electronic-delivery consent on file is annuity-specific and current before choosing the electronic channel.
checklist.done: each pack has a stored sent image and a tracking or envelope reference on the notice log row.

checklist.step: Start and record the free-look clock on delivery, not on issue
actions: Read the carrier delivery date or the DocuSign completion timestamp and enter it as the Contract Delivery Date on the contract record.
Let the system compute Free-Look Expiry = delivery date + the state's free-look days for that channel, and check the days used match the state variation grid maintained under REG-011-C01.
Suppress surrender charges and lock the refund basis (purchase payments or account value per the state) until the expiry date.
Where the carrier reports no delivery within 10 calendar days, treat the pack as undelivered and re-issue rather than letting the clock run from the mail date.
checklist.done: every contract shows a sourced delivery date, a computed free-look expiry using the state's own days, and a locked refund basis.

checklist.step: Work the undeliverable and returned-mail queue daily
actions: Pull the returned-mail and bounced-email report each morning and match each item to a contract number on the notice log.
Trace a good address through the producer of record and the Customer Self-Service Portal profile, and update the address of record on the contract.
Re-mail the full pack, not just the covering letter, and reset the Contract Delivery Date and the free-look expiry from the new delivery date.
Escalate any item unresolved after two attempts to the Annuity Service Specialist for producer and telephone follow-up.
checklist.done: no returned pack sits unworked beyond two business days and every re-mail resets the delivery date and free-look expiry.

checklist.step: Deliver the group annuity certificate disclosure to certificate holders
actions: For each group annuity contract, identify the certificate holders who pay the consideration, since those are the persons the disclosure obligation attaches to.
Agree with the plan sponsor contact the enrolment channel and whether the sponsor or the carrier distributes the disclosure and Buyer's Guide, and record that in the case file.
Where the sponsor distributes, obtain a dated distribution confirmation naming the disclosure form number and Buyer's Guide edition, and log it as the proof of delivery.
Where the carrier distributes, mail directly to the certificate holder and log the same evidence as for individual contracts.
checklist.done: every group certificate holder has a logged delivery with a named distributor and a dated confirmation.

checklist.step: Run the Section 5 annual report on the anniversary cycle
actions: Run the monthly anniversary extract of all in-force deferred annuity contracts reaching a contract anniversary in the month.
Generate the annual report showing beginning and end of period contract value, gross purchase payments received, interest credited, charges deducted, withdrawals, surrender value and death benefit.
Check the run count against the in-force count for that anniversary month and investigate any contract that dropped out of the run before mailing.
Release the run for print or e-delivery so it reaches owners within 30 days of the anniversary date.
checklist.done: the anniversary run reconciles to the in-force count and is released in time to land within 30 days of anniversary.

checklist.step: Answer on-request current value enquiries inside the service level
actions: Log every request for current contract values with contract number, requester identity verification result and request date.
Pull the current values screen from the policy administration record and issue the statement in writing, not verbally only, within 10 business days.
Attach the issued statement image to the contract record and add a notice log row so the on-request delivery is evidenced like any other.
Route any request that also alleges the owner never received the original disclosure to the Complaints Specialist under REG-011-C05 the same day.
checklist.done: every value request has a logged date, a written response inside 10 business days and an attached statement image.

checklist.step: Reconcile the notice log to issued contracts every week
actions: Extract all annuity contracts issued in the week and left-join to the notice log on contract number.
List contracts with no disclosure row, no Buyer's Guide row, or no acknowledgement image, and work each one to closure inside the week.
List acknowledgement dates later than application signature dates for face-to-face sales and pass each to the Producer Compliance Manager for producer follow-up.
Publish the weekly gap count and ageing to the Policy Admin Ops Lead.
checklist.done: the weekly reconciliation runs, gaps are worked inside the week, and the gap count is published.

checklist.step: Remediate a late or missing delivery properly
actions: For each confirmed gap, send the missing disclosure or Buyer's Guide by tracked mail with a covering letter naming what was omitted.
Where the omission affected the owner's free-look decision, re-open the free-look period from the new delivery date and suppress surrender charges for that window.
Record on the contract the gap in days, the corrective mailing date, the new free-look expiry and the decision maker.
Refer any pattern involving one producer or one agency to the Producer Compliance Manager for a conduct review.
checklist.done: every gap has a tracked corrective mailing, a documented free-look decision and a named decision maker.

checklist.step: Feed producer-level delivery failures into distribution oversight
actions: Aggregate acknowledgement failures by producer National Producer Number and agency for the rolling quarter.
Confirm the producer's appointment and licence status in NIPR for the state of solicitation before opening a conduct discussion.
Issue a written expectation letter at the first failure and place repeat producers on a pre-issue review requiring the acknowledgement image before any case is accepted.
Record the action and the review-off date on the producer file.
checklist.done: every repeat-failing producer has a written action and, where warranted, a pre-issue review flag with a review-off date.

checklist.step: Report delivery performance to the Compliance Committee monthly
actions: Publish the monthly pack: acknowledgement-on-time rate for face-to-face sales, pack completeness rate for non-face-to-face sales, annual report within-30-days rate, and open gaps by ageing bucket.
Split the metrics by state so a jurisdiction with a longer free-look or a state-specific guide is visible on its own.
Name every contract still open past 30 days with its owner and its promised close date.
Send the pack to the Head of Compliance three business days before the committee sits.
checklist.done: the monthly pack is published with state splits and a named owner against every gap open past 30 days.

checklist.step: Preserve delivery evidence against the retention rule
actions: Confirm every notice log row links to the sent PDF image, the signed acknowledgement image and the carrier or envelope tracking reference.
Apply the retention label of three years from contract termination or the conclusion of the next market conduct examination, whichever is later.
Run a quarterly integrity check that a random 25 contract numbers each retrieve all three artefacts within one minute.
Escalate any unretrievable artefact to the Policy Admin Ops Lead as an evidence defect.
checklist.done: every logged delivery retrieves its sent image, acknowledgement and tracking reference, with retention applied.

checklist.step: Refresh the state delivery rules whenever the variation grid changes
actions: Subscribe the delivery procedure to the regulatory library entry for Annuity Disclosure (NAIC Model 245) so any state amendment raises a task.
On each change, update the free-look days, refund basis and channel delivery point in the delivery procedure and notify the Policy Issuance Specialist and Configuration Engineer the same week.
Re-issue the one-page channel decision tree to the new business floor and the contact centre.
Record the effective date of the change and the first contract issued under the new rule.
checklist.done: every state rule change reaches the procedure, the floor and the configuration team with an effective date recorded.

testing.step: Build the population of applications, issues and anniversaries for the period
actions: Extract every annuity application received and every contract issued in the period with contract number, product, state of solicitation, sale method, application signature date, issue date and contract delivery date.
Extract every in-force contract with an anniversary in the period as the Section 5 annual report population.
Reconcile the issued-contract count to the new business production report and the anniversary count to the in-force listing, and resolve differences before sampling.
testing.done: both populations reconcile to production and in-force reports and are signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile every issued contract to a complete notice log row
actions: Left-join the issued-contract population to the notice log on contract number.
Flag as automatic exceptions any contract with no disclosure row, no Buyer's Guide row, no acknowledgement image, or no delivery tracking reference.
Count exceptions by state and by channel so a single broken workflow branch is visible rather than averaged away.
Carry the exception list into the sample as mandatory rows.
testing.done: every issued contract matches a complete notice log row or sits on the exception list with a state and channel tag.

testing.step: Draw a stratified, reproducible sample of contracts and anniversaries
actions: Stratify by sale method (face-to-face, mail, telephone, internet) and take at least 15 contracts from each stratum that has volume.
Add 100% of the reconciliation exception rows and 10 group annuity certificate deliveries.
Add 25 anniversaries from the annual report population, selected at random with a recorded seed.
Record the seed, stratum sizes and draw date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is stratified by channel, includes all exceptions and group certificates, and is reproducible from the recorded seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the at-or-before-application test on face-to-face sales
actions: Open the imaged acknowledgement for each sampled face-to-face contract and read the receipt date from the form itself, not from the indexed field.
Compare it to the application signature date on the imaged application and compute the difference in days.
Any positive difference is a Model 245 Section 4B(1) failure; record the days late and the producer National Producer Number.
Confirm the acknowledgement names the disclosure form number, edition date and Buyer's Guide edition actually mailed, and treat a blank or generic acknowledgement as a failure.
testing.done: each sampled face-to-face contract has a recomputed day difference from the imaged documents and a pass or fail conclusion.

testing.step: Open the sent image for non-face-to-face packs and test completeness
actions: Retrieve the exact PDF image sent for each sampled non-face-to-face contract from the document repository.
Confirm the pack contains the contract, data pages, the state-approved disclosure edition, the correct Buyer's Guide edition and the free-look notice.
Read the disclosure form number and edition date off the footer and confirm it was approved for that state on the issue date.
A pack missing the Buyer's Guide is a reportable breach, not a documentation exception.
testing.done: every sampled non-face-to-face pack image is opened and its five components individually confirmed or failed.

testing.step: Recompute the free-look expiry from the delivery evidence
actions: Take the carrier delivery date or DocuSign completion timestamp for each sampled contract as the start date, ignoring the recorded field.
Look up the state's free-look days for that channel in the variation grid and independently confirm them against the state's adopting text (representative: Alaska adoption of NAIC Model 245).
Recompute expiry = delivery date + state days and compare to the value on the contract, applying the 15-day non-face-to-face floor.
Test that surrender charges were actually suppressed to the recomputed expiry by reading the charge configuration on the contract.
testing.done: every sampled free-look expiry is recomputed from delivery evidence and reconciles, or the shortfall in days is recorded.

testing.step: Test annual report timeliness and content against Section 5
actions: For each sampled anniversary, retrieve the annual report image and compute days from anniversary date to send date against the 30-day standard.
Confirm the report shows beginning and end of period contract value, gross purchase payments, interest credited, charges deducted, withdrawals, surrender value and death benefit.
Tie the end-of-period contract value on the report to the policy administration value at the anniversary date to the cent.
List any anniversary with no report generated as an automatic exception with the contract number.
testing.done: every sampled anniversary has a recomputed day count, a Section 5 field check and a value tie to the admin record.

testing.step: Test the returned-mail and re-delivery loop end to end
actions: Extract the period's returned-mail and bounced-email items and match each to a contract number.
For 15 items, trace the re-mail: new address source, re-mail date, tracked delivery confirmation and the reset of Contract Delivery Date and free-look expiry.
Flag any item where the free-look clock continued to run from the original mail date despite non-delivery.
Flag any item unresolved past two attempts with no escalation record.
testing.done: every traced returned item shows a re-mail, a reset delivery date and a reset free-look expiry, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one case per exception carrying contract number, state, channel, the delivery gap in days and the producer National Producer Number where relevant.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: sale method misclassified, acknowledgement not collected, pack component missing, delivery date sourced from mail date, anniversary run dropout, returned mail unworked.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and open a free-look re-opening decision for any gap that could have affected the owner's cancellation right.
Refer producer-driven root causes to the Producer Compliance Manager and carry every open case into next month's test.
testing.done: every exception has a case, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, where relevant, a free-look decision.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the delivery test
actions: Compute the acknowledgement-on-time rate, pack completeness rate and annual report within-30-days rate and compare each to its threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references for each failed contract.
Have the independent reviewer, who processed and mailed none of the sampled contracts, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any re-opened free-look periods to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, the three rates and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Convert the disclosure rules into numbered system requirements
actions: Open the Annuity Disclosure Delivery Procedure and the 45-jurisdiction variation grid and write one numbered requirement per testable rule.

Write the delivery requirements explicitly: face-to-face sales must block issue until an acknowledgement dated on or before the application signature date exists; non-face-to-face sales must attach disclosure, Buyer's Guide and free-look notice to the contract delivery package.

Write the calculation requirements: free-look expiry equals contract delivery date plus the state and channel value from the parameter table, never a house default, never below 15 days for non-face-to-face sales.

Write the Section 5 requirement: generate the annual report for every in-force deferred annuity contract at each anniversary with the seven required value fields, released to reach the owner within 30 days.
Have the Compliance Manager confirm each requirement traces to a Model 245 section before development starts.
checklist.done: every rule has a numbered, testable requirement carrying its Model 245 section reference and a Compliance confirmation.

checklist.step: Load and version the 45-state parameter table
actions: Create one row per state and channel holding free-look days, refund basis (purchase payments or account value), delivery point (at or before application versus with contract), enhanced senior free-look days and the effective-from date.
Populate the values from the Compliance-maintained variation grid by controlled import, never by hand keying, and store the import file as evidence.
Set an effective-dated structure so a future state change can be loaded ahead of its effective date without affecting current business.
Run the import report and reconcile row count and every value back to the grid line by line with the Compliance Analyst.
checklist.done: the parameter table holds effective-dated rows for all 45 jurisdictions and reconciles value for value to the variation grid.

checklist.step: Configure the sale-method branch in the new business workflow
actions: Make Sale Method a mandatory, validated field on the annuity application screen with the values Face-to-face, Mail, Telephone and Internet.
Branch the workflow so the face-to-face path raises an Acknowledgement Required activity that blocks the issue transition until an acknowledgement document is attached and dated.
Branch the non-face-to-face path to add the disclosure, Buyer's Guide and free-look notice to the contract delivery package composition.
Prevent the field being edited after issue except through an audited correction transaction so the branch cannot be rewritten retrospectively.
checklist.done: Sale Method is mandatory and audited, and each value drives its own enforced workflow branch.

checklist.step: Build the document trigger rules per product and state
actions: Define a trigger for each required document: disclosure document, Buyer's Guide, free-look notice, acknowledgement and annual report.
Key each trigger on product, state of solicitation, sale method and transaction event so a live product/state pair cannot exist without a trigger.
Point each trigger at the form number and edition date held in the form inventory rather than at a hard-coded file, so a REG-011-C01 edition change flows through without a code release.
Add a hard failure — not a warning — when a trigger cannot resolve a document, so the package stops rather than mailing incomplete.
checklist.done: every live product/state/channel combination resolves all required documents, and unresolved triggers hard-stop the package.

checklist.step: Implement the free-look calculation and the surrender charge suppression
actions: Wire Contract Delivery Date to the carrier delivery feed and the DocuSign completion webhook so it cannot be set from the print date.
Implement expiry = Contract Delivery Date + parameter table days for the state and channel, with a floor of 15 days where sale method is not Face-to-face.
Suppress surrender charges and market value adjustment on any full surrender processed on or before the expiry date, and apply the state's refund basis.
Write the computed expiry, the parameter values used and the parameter table version onto the contract record so the calculation can be audited after the fact.
checklist.done: free-look expiry is computed from delivery evidence with the state parameters stamped on the contract and charges suppressed to expiry.

checklist.step: Schedule and instrument the Section 5 anniversary job
actions: Schedule the anniversary extract to run monthly on a fixed working day with a lead time that lets print and mail land inside 30 days of anniversary.
Build the job to select every in-force deferred annuity contract with an anniversary in the window and to write a row per contract into the notice log whether or not the document generated.
Emit a reconciliation record for each run: contracts selected, documents generated, documents suppressed and the reason for each suppression.
Fail the run loudly to the Production Support Analyst when generated count is below selected count rather than completing silently.
checklist.done: the job runs on schedule, writes a notice log row per selected contract, and fails visibly on any generation shortfall.

checklist.step: Write the regression pack that proves the rules before every release
actions: Build one automated case per numbered requirement, linked to the requirement id so coverage gaps are visible.

Include boundary cases: acknowledgement dated the same day as the application (pass), one day later (fail and block), non-face-to-face state with a 10-day statutory free-look (must apply the 15-day floor), and a state with an enhanced senior period.
Include a negative case where the form inventory returns no edition for a state — the package must hard-stop, not mail a partial pack.
Include a Section 5 case asserting all seven value fields populate and the end-of-period value ties to the admin value at the anniversary date.
checklist.done: every requirement id has at least one automated case, including the boundary and negative cases named above.

checklist.step: Execute the regression pack in a state-representative test environment
actions: Refresh the test environment with masked production annuity data covering at least ten states, including Alaska, Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona.
Run the full pack and record pass, fail and blocked counts against each requirement id.
Open a defect for every failure with the requirement id, the state, the expected and actual values, and the affected trigger or parameter row.
Re-run the failed subset after each fix and keep the run history on the release record rather than overwriting it.
checklist.done: the pack has run to a recorded result per requirement id with defects raised and re-run evidence retained.

checklist.step: Have Compliance test the state parameter values independently
actions: Export the parameter table from the test environment and compare it row by row to the current variation grid for all 45 jurisdictions.

Pick ten states and re-read their adopting text to confirm the free-look days and refund basis, using the Alaska adoption of NAIC Model 245 and the Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona adoptions as the anchor set.
Reject the release for any single value mismatch — a wrong free-look day count is a consumer-facing breach, not a defect to defer.
Sign the parameter reconciliation and attach it to the change ticket.
checklist.done: a signed 45-state parameter reconciliation is attached to the change ticket with zero unexplained mismatches.

checklist.step: Take the change through the change advisory gate
actions: Raise the change record with the requirement ids, the regulatory effective date, the regression results and the signed parameter reconciliation attached.
Confirm the mandatory approvals are present: Business Systems Analyst, Test Lead, Compliance Manager and Head of IT.
Set the implementation window so the change lands on or before the regulatory effective date, and record the back-out plan and its tested restore point.
Block scheduling where the Compliance sign-off is missing rather than approving conditionally.
checklist.done: the change is scheduled only with all four approvals, a dated back-out plan and a window inside the regulatory effective date.

checklist.step: Deploy and verify in production the same day
actions: Deploy the configuration and record the deployment id, timestamp and the parameter table version now live.
Run the post-deployment smoke set: issue one test case per sale method in three states and open the generated package to confirm all components resolved.
Read back the computed free-look expiry on each smoke case and confirm it matches the state parameter value.
Invoke the back-out plan immediately on any smoke failure rather than fixing forward in production.
checklist.done: deployment is recorded and the smoke set confirms component resolution and free-look computation in production.

checklist.step: Monitor the first production cycle for mis-triggers
actions: Watch the daily package-composition dashboard for 10 business days after release for missing-component hard stops, unresolved triggers and free-look values outside the expected range for the state.
Compare daily issued-contract counts to daily notice log row counts and investigate any gap the same day.
Raise a Priority 2 incident on the first mis-trigger with the count of contracts already affected.
Hand every affected contract number to the Compliance Analyst for the remediation mailing under REG-011-C02.
checklist.done: the first ten business days are monitored daily with any mis-trigger raised as a P2 and affected contracts handed to Compliance.

checklist.step: Keep the requirement-to-rule traceability matrix current
actions: Update the matrix so each Model 245 requirement maps to the live trigger id, parameter table column, calculation rule and automated test case id.
Mark any requirement with no live rule as an open control gap with an owner and a target date, visible to the Head of Compliance.
Review the matrix at every quarterly release planning session and after any platform upgrade.
Publish the matrix version alongside the parameter table version so an examiner can see what was live on any given date.
checklist.done: the matrix maps every requirement to a live rule and test case, with open gaps owned and dated.

checklist.step: Retire superseded configuration cleanly
actions: End-date the superseded parameter rows and trigger rules rather than deleting them so the historical rule set can be reproduced for an examination.
Confirm no live product/state pair now points at an end-dated rule by running the trigger coverage report.
Archive the superseded configuration export with its effective window into the evidence repository.
Notify the Policy Admin Ops Lead of the changeover date so the operational procedure and the system agree.
checklist.done: superseded rules are end-dated not deleted, coverage shows no orphaned product/state pair, and the archive is filed.

checklist.step: File the configuration evidence pack
actions: Assemble the pack: requirement list, traceability matrix version, parameter table export and reconciliation, regression results, change approvals, deployment record and smoke results.
Apply the three-years-or-next-examination retention label and index by release date and parameter table version.
Record the pack location on the change ticket and close the ticket.
Confirm with the Records Manager that the pack is retrievable by release date and by state.
checklist.done: a single indexed configuration evidence pack per release is filed with retention applied and its location on the ticket.

testing.step: Build the population of annuity disclosure configuration changes for the period
actions: Extract every change record in the period touching annuity document triggers, the state parameter table, the free-look calculation or the anniversary scheduler.
Add the deployment log from the release pipeline so a configuration edit made outside change control is exposed.
Reconcile the two lists and treat any deployment with no change record as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the change population is reconciled to the deployment log and signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the live parameter table to the Compliance variation grid for all 45 states
actions: Export the production parameter table as at period end with effective dates.
Compare every row to the Compliance variation grid on free-look days, refund basis, delivery point and enhanced senior period.
Confirm no row carries free-look days below 15 for a non-face-to-face channel.
List every mismatch with the state, the field, the live value and the required value — no materiality filter.
testing.done: all 45 jurisdictions are compared field by field and every mismatch is listed with both values.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of changes and product/state pairs
actions: Take 100% of changes that altered a free-look value, a delivery point or a hard-stop rule.
Take 10 further changes at random with a recorded seed, plus 20 live product/state/channel combinations selected across at least eight states.
Record the seed, population sizes and draw date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and includes every change that touched a free-look or delivery rule.

testing.step: Re-perform trigger coverage for each sampled product/state/channel pair
actions: For each sampled combination, query the trigger configuration and list the documents that would resolve for a new issue today.
Confirm the disclosure document, Buyer's Guide, free-look notice and acknowledgement all resolve, and that each resolves to a form number and edition date that is current in the form inventory.
Force an unresolvable case by pointing at a retired edition in the test environment and confirm the package hard-stops rather than mailing partial.
Any combination missing a document, or resolving a retired edition, is an exception with the volume of business written on that pair.
testing.done: each sampled combination has an independent coverage result and the hard-stop behaviour is demonstrated.

testing.step: Recompute the free-look calculation independently in the test environment
actions: Create test contracts in at least six states across all four sale methods with known delivery dates.
Compute the expected expiry by hand from the state's adopting text (Alaska adoption of NAIC Model 245 as the anchor) rather than from the parameter table, applying the 15-day non-face-to-face floor.
Compare to the system-computed expiry and record any difference in days.
Process a full surrender one day before expiry on three cases and confirm the surrender charge and market value adjustment were suppressed and the state's refund basis applied.
testing.done: hand-computed and system-computed expiries agree for every test case and charge suppression is demonstrated.

testing.step: Prove the acknowledgement gate actually blocks issue
actions: Attempt to issue a face-to-face test case with no acknowledgement attached and confirm the transition is blocked, not warned.
Attempt to issue a case whose acknowledgement is dated one day after the application signature date and confirm it is blocked and routed to the Not In Good Order queue.
Attempt to edit Sale Method after issue and confirm the edit is either refused or written to the audit trail with user and timestamp.
Capture screenshots of each attempt into the workpaper.
testing.done: all three gate attempts behave as required with captured evidence, or the gap is raised as an exception.

testing.step: Test the Section 5 anniversary job for completeness and timing
actions: Pull the last three monthly run records: contracts selected, documents generated, documents suppressed and suppression reasons.
Reconcile contracts selected to the independent in-force anniversary count from the data warehouse for the same months.
Sample 15 suppressions and confirm each has a legitimate reason recorded rather than a silent drop.
Compute the interval from anniversary date to release date for each run and compare to the 30-day standard.
testing.done: each run reconciles to the independent anniversary count, suppressions are justified and the 30-day interval is recomputed.

testing.step: Test change control on the sampled changes
actions: For each sampled change, confirm the four approvals exist and pre-date the deployment timestamp.
Confirm the signed 45-state parameter reconciliation and the regression results are attached, and that the regression covers the requirement ids the change touched.
Compare the deployment date to the regulatory effective date recorded on the ticket and flag any change that landed late.
A change deployed with a Compliance approval added after the deployment timestamp is a control failure, not a paperwork gap.
testing.done: every sampled change shows four pre-dated approvals, attached test evidence and an on-time deployment, or an exception.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one incident per exception with the state, the product/state pair or change id, the defective rule and the count of contracts issued under it.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: parameter value wrong, trigger missing, hard-stop downgraded to a warning, delivery date sourced from print, scheduler dropout, approval bypassed.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and hand affected contract numbers to Policy Administration for corrective mailing under REG-011-C02.
Carry every open incident into the next release test as a mandatory retest.
testing.done: every exception has an incident, a contract count, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the configuration test
actions: Compute the parameter mismatch count, the trigger coverage gap count and the change control failure count against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references and the affected contract volumes.
Have the independent reviewer, who wrote, reviewed and deployed none of the sampled configuration, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and the Head of IT, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, the three counts and a reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Re-verify the source rules before rewriting the course
actions: Open the regulatory library entry for Annuity Disclosure (NAIC Model 245) and pull every change logged since the last annual release.
Re-read Model 245 Section 4B, 4C and Section 5 and the representative state adoptions — Alaska, plus Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona — and note any amended free-look period or delivery point.
Check whether the NAIC has revised the Buyer's Guide for Deferred Annuities since the last release and whether any state has mandated its own guide.
Write a one-page change note listing what must change in the course, and send it to the Instructional Designer as the content brief.
checklist.done: a dated change note exists naming every rule change that must reach the course this cycle.

checklist.step: Define the in-scope audience by job code, not by team name
actions: List the job codes that touch annuity disclosure: new business case management, policy issuance, annuity servicing, contact centre annuity queues, complaints, producer compliance and the annuity forms team.
Pull the worker list for those codes from the HRIS feed including contractors, secondees and anyone on a temporary assignment.
Agree the inclusion rule with the Chief HR Officer's delegate in writing so audit can test the boundary rather than argue it.
Publish the audience definition with an effective date and store it with the course record.
checklist.done: the audience is defined by job code with contractors included and the definition is published with an effective date.

checklist.step: Write the delivery-timing module against Section 4B
actions: Teach the two delivery rules side by side: face-to-face sales require the disclosure document and Buyer's Guide at or before the time of application; mail, telephone and internet sales require them no later than contract delivery with an unconditional refund right of at least 15 days.
Show a real acknowledgement form on screen with the receipt date field circled and explain why it must be earlier than or equal to the application signature date.
Include the group annuity case where the certificate holder pays the consideration and the disclosure attaches to the certificate holder.
Write four scenario questions with wrong answers drawn from the exceptions actually logged last year, not from invented mistakes.
checklist.done: the module teaches both delivery rules, shows the live acknowledgement form and carries four scenario questions grounded in real exceptions.

checklist.step: Write the content and Buyer's Guide module against Section 4C
actions: Walk the learner through the live disclosure document page by page, naming each Section 4C element: long-term-nature statement, guaranteed and non-guaranteed elements, crediting method, surrender and withdrawal charges and their period, market value adjustment, all fees and rider charges, annuitization options and the 10% early-distribution tax penalty.
Teach the Buyer's Guide edition rule — fixed, indexed or variable — and how to check the paired edition in the form inventory before sending.
Include the rule that current values must be provided on request and how to log that delivery.
Add a short exercise where the learner spots the missing element in a deliberately defective sample pack.
checklist.done: the module covers every Section 4C element against the live document and includes the defective-pack exercise.

checklist.step: Build the state variation module for the 45 jurisdictions
actions: Turn the Compliance variation grid into a searchable job aid showing free-look days by state and channel, refund basis and enhanced senior periods.
Teach the rule that the state of solicitation, not the residence state, drives the requirement, and that the system parameter table is the operational source.
Call out the states whose free-look or refund basis differs most from the house norm so the learner remembers to check rather than assume.
Attach the job aid as a downloadable one-pager the learner keeps at the desk.
checklist.done: the state module ships with a searchable 45-state job aid and teaches the state-of-solicitation rule.

checklist.step: Build role-specific tracks rather than one generic course
actions: Create a new business track ending in the acknowledgement gate, an issuance track ending in pack composition, a servicing track ending in the Section 5 annual report and on-request values, and a complaints track ending in root cause coding.
Keep the Section 4B and 4C modules common to all tracks so the core rules are taught identically.
Map each track to the job codes from the audience definition.
Set the target duration per track at no more than 45 minutes so completion is realistic during peak new business volume.
checklist.done: four role tracks exist, share the common core modules and are mapped to job codes with a stated duration.

checklist.step: Set the assessment and the pass rule
actions: Build a 15-question assessment per track drawn from a larger item bank so retakes are not the same paper.
Set the pass mark at 80% with two retake attempts and a mandatory manager conversation before a third attempt.
Include at least three questions that require reading the state job aid to answer correctly.
Add the end-of-course attestation confirming the learner will not release an annuity issue without the required delivery evidence.
checklist.done: each track has an item-bank assessment, an 80% pass mark, two retakes and a captured attestation.

checklist.step: Get the content approved before release
actions: Review the course against the change note and confirm every rule change reached the content.
Have Regulatory Counsel read the delivery-timing and state variation modules and confirm no statement understates a state requirement.
Record the content version, the approval date and the approvers on the course record.
Reject release where any module still cites a superseded free-look period or a retired Buyer's Guide edition.
checklist.done: the course carries a versioned, dated approval from Compliance and Counsel with no superseded citations.

checklist.step: Assign the curriculum and open the annual window
actions: Release the course by 31 January and auto-assign by job code from the HRIS feed with a 31 March due date.
Configure the joiner and mover rule so any worker entering an in-scope job code is assigned automatically with a 30-day due date.
Set reminders at assignment and at 30, 14, 7 and 1 days before the due date, and weekly overdue notices to the learner and line manager afterwards.
Publish the assigned headcount by department to the Head of Compliance on release day as the baseline for completion tracking.
checklist.done: the course is live by 31 January, auto-assigned by job code, with the joiner rule and the reminder ladder configured.

checklist.step: Run the completion campaign to the due date
actions: Publish weekly completion percentages by department and by manager from February onward.
Send named overdue lists to each department head with the individuals, not just the counts.
Chase every learner with two failed attempts individually and book the manager conversation before the third attempt.
Escalate any department below 90% at 14 days before the due date to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: weekly named tracking runs from February and every sub-90% department is escalated before the due date.

checklist.step: Enforce the consequence for anyone still overdue
actions: On 1 April, take the overdue list and confirm with the Policy Admin Ops Lead which of those workers hold annuity new business or servicing entitlements.
Suspend the annuity issue and servicing entitlement for anyone overdue past 60 days and record the suspension date on the exception.
Approve or refuse each deferral request in writing, with a maximum extension of 30 days and a stated business reason.
Restore entitlements only on completion evidence from the LMS, never on a manager's assurance.
checklist.done: every learner overdue past 60 days has either a written deferral or a recorded entitlement suspension.

checklist.step: Run out-of-cycle training when a state rule moves
actions: On any state amendment to its Model 245 adoption, or any NAIC Buyer's Guide revision, draft a bulletin naming the state, the old and new requirement and the effective date.
Release it as a mandatory 10-minute micro-module to the affected tracks with a 30-day due date.
Update the state job aid and re-issue it so the desk copy is never behind the system parameter table.
Report the bulletin completion rate to the Head of Compliance at the 30-day mark.
checklist.done: each rule change has a dated micro-module, an updated job aid and a reported 30-day completion rate.

checklist.step: Cover producers as well as employees
actions: Publish the disclosure delivery requirements, the acknowledgement form and the state free-look job aid to the producer portal at each annual release.
Confirm through NIPR that appointed producers writing annuity business in each state hold the state's required annuity training credit before releasing new business codes.
Send the annual disclosure bulletin to every appointed annuity producer and record the distribution list and date.
Feed producers with repeated acknowledgement failures into a mandatory re-training requirement before further business is accepted.
checklist.done: producers have the current materials, verified state annuity training credit and a re-training path for repeat failures.

checklist.step: Certify completion at the annual close
actions: Reconcile the LMS completion register to the HRIS population as at 31 March and again at 31 December, listing every unmatched worker.
Prepare the completion certification stating assigned headcount, completed headcount, completion rate, average score and the open exceptions with owners.
Have the Head of Compliance sign the certification.
Present it to the Compliance Committee with the exception list attached.
checklist.done: a signed completion certification with a reconciled headcount and named open exceptions is presented to the committee.

checklist.step: File the training evidence pack
actions: Assemble the pack: course content version and approval record, audience definition, assignment roster, completion and score register, attestations, bulletins, deferrals and entitlement suspensions.
Apply the three-years-or-next-examination retention label and index by cycle year and job code.
Confirm a named individual's completion record and score can be retrieved in under a minute for an examiner request.
Record the pack location on the course record.
checklist.done: the annual pack is filed, retention-labelled and a named individual's record is retrievable in under a minute.

testing.step: Build the in-scope worker population independently of the LMS
actions: Extract from HRIS every active worker at period end whose job code appears in the published audience definition, including contractors and secondees.
Add every worker who held an in-scope job code at any point in the cycle even if they have since moved, since they processed annuity business while in scope.
Reconcile the headcount to the department headcount report and resolve differences before sampling.
testing.done: the population is built from HRIS, includes leavers and movers within the cycle, and reconciles to department headcount.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the LMS assignment and completion register
actions: Left-join the HRIS population to the LMS assignment register on worker id and list everyone in scope with no assignment.
Left-join to the completion register and list everyone assigned with no completion by 31 March, with days overdue.
Cross-check the reverse direction: completions recorded for workers not in the audience definition, which usually means the assignment rule is mis-scoped.
Treat every unassigned in-scope worker as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every in-scope worker matches an assignment and a completion, or appears on the exception list with days overdue.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of learners and content
actions: Take 100% of the unassigned and overdue exception rows.
Take 30 completed learners at random with a recorded seed, stratified so each of the four role tracks is represented.
Take the current content version of each track plus the state job aid for content testing.
Record the seed, population size and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all exceptions and includes each role track's content version.

testing.step: Re-perform the content accuracy check against the regulation
actions: Read the delivery-timing module against Model 245 Section 4B and confirm it states the at-or-before-application rule for face-to-face sales and the contract-delivery rule with a minimum 15-day refund right otherwise.
Check the Section 4C module names every required disclosure element with none omitted or softened.
Test ten states on the job aid — starting with Alaska and including Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona — against their adopting text and confirm the free-look days and refund basis are current.
A course teaching a superseded free-look period is a fail regardless of completion rate.
testing.done: each module is confirmed against the regulation and ten job-aid states are verified against their adopting text.

testing.step: Verify completion records for the sampled learners
actions: Open each sampled learner's record and read the completion date, the score, the number of attempts and the content version completed.
Confirm the completion date is on or before 31 March, or within 30 days of the job code effective date for joiners and movers.
Confirm the content version completed is the current cycle's version, not a carried-forward prior-year completion.
Confirm the attestation was captured and treat a completion with no attestation as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled learner shows an in-date completion on the current content version with a score, attempt count and attestation.

testing.step: Test that the assessment actually discriminates
actions: Pull the item-level statistics for each track: percentage correct per question and average attempts to pass.
Flag any question answered correctly by over 98% of learners as non-discriminating and any below 40% as ambiguous.
Confirm the three state job-aid questions exist and that learners who failed them were required to retake rather than passing on the aggregate.
Confirm retake papers draw from the item bank and are not identical to the first attempt.
testing.done: item statistics are reviewed, non-discriminating and ambiguous questions are flagged, and retake variation is confirmed.

testing.step: Trace training back to behaviour in the operational exceptions
actions: Take the delivery exceptions logged under REG-011-C02 for the period and list the individuals who processed them.
Check each individual's completion status and score at the date of the exception.
Where the individual was trained and current, record it as a training-effectiveness finding pointing at content or process rather than at completion.
Where the individual was untrained or overdue, record it as a control failure with the manager named.
testing.done: every delivery exception is mapped to the performer's training status at the time and classified as effectiveness or control failure.

testing.step: Test enforcement of the overdue consequence
actions: Take everyone overdue past 60 days and pull their annuity new business and servicing entitlements as at the suspension date.
Confirm the entitlement was actually suspended and check whether they processed any annuity transaction after the 60-day point.
Confirm every deferral has a written approval from the Head of Compliance with a business reason and a maximum 30-day extension.
Any transaction processed by a suspended-but-not-actually-suspended worker is a reportable control failure.
testing.done: every 60-day overdue worker shows a real entitlement suspension or an approved deferral, with no post-suspension transactions.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with the worker or content item, the department, the gap and whether annuity business was processed while non-current.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: job code not in the audience definition, joiner rule missed, manager did not release time, content out of date, entitlement suspension not applied.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and for content exceptions require an out-of-cycle micro-module rather than waiting for next year.
Carry every open issue into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the training test
actions: Compute the completion rate against the 100%-by-31-March standard and the average score against the 80% pass mark.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the content findings and the untrained-performer findings separately.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither built nor assigned the course, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee alongside the signed completion certification and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, the completion rate, average score and a committee reporting date exists.

In-scope systems.value: Complaint case file with reason and sub-reason coding, state, contract number, DOI file number, deadline clock and the root-cause and remediation fields
