checklist.step: Capture every annuity complaint into one register whatever the channel
actions: Open a case for every expression of dissatisfaction about an annuity received by DOI referral, letter, email, the Customer Self-Service Portal, the contact centre or a producer, and record the channel.
Record contract number, owner name, state of solicitation, product, producer National Producer Number, receipt date and, for DOI referrals, the department file number and the department letter date.
Pull the contact centre interaction record from Genesys Cloud for telephone complaints and attach the call reference and recording id.
Never close a matter at first call without a case; the register is the evidence base for the Market Conduct Annual Statement.
checklist.done: every annuity complaint has a case with channel, state, contract number, receipt date and, for DOI referrals, the department file number.

checklist.step: Code the complaint against the Model 245 reason set
actions: Apply a reason code from the disclosure set: disclosure document not received, Buyer's Guide not received, received after application, free-look period misstated or refused, surrender charges not disclosed, market value adjustment not disclosed, annual report not received, values on request not provided.
Add the general market conduct category (Marketing and Sales, Policyholder Service, Underwriting) so the case maps to the MCAS annuity reason taxonomy.
Where the complainant's wording is vague, read the letter for the substance rather than the label and code what is actually alleged.
Add a second code where a complaint spans both content and delivery so trending does not lose one of them.
checklist.done: every case carries a specific disclosure reason code, an MCAS-mappable category and a second code where the allegation is dual.

checklist.step: Pull the delivery evidence before answering anything
actions: Retrieve from the notice log the disclosure and Buyer's Guide rows for the contract: form number, edition date, send date, channel and tracking or envelope reference.
Retrieve the imaged acknowledgement and read the receipt date and both signatures off the image itself.
Retrieve the exact sent PDF image from the document repository and confirm it contains the components the complainant says were missing.
Where any artefact cannot be retrieved, treat the complaint as substantiated on the evidence available rather than assuming delivery occurred.
checklist.done: the case file holds the notice log rows, the acknowledgement image and the sent pack image, or records that they could not be retrieved.

checklist.step: Test the allegation against the actual state requirement
actions: Look up the state of solicitation in the variation grid and confirm the free-look days and refund basis that applied on the contract's delivery date.

Recompute delivery timing: for face-to-face sales compare the acknowledgement receipt date to the application signature date, for other channels compare the pack delivery date to the contract delivery date and the 15-day floor.
Read the sent disclosure edition against the Section 4C element list for the specific element the complainant says was missing.
Write a substantiated or not-substantiated conclusion with the dates and the citation, for the representative jurisdiction Alaska adoption of NAIC Model 245 or the applicable state adoption.
checklist.done: each case carries a dated, cited substantiation conclusion built from recomputed timing and the actual sent document.

checklist.step: Run the DOI response clock from the department letter date
actions: Enter the department letter date, not the internal receipt date, and let the case compute the due date from the state's stated response window.
Confirm the window against the department's own letter, since several states shorten it for annuity and senior consumer matters.
Set the escalation flags at 50% and 80% of the window and route to the Complaints Manager automatically at 80%.
Request an extension in writing from the analyst named on the department letter where evidence retrieval will genuinely overrun, and record the department's reply.
checklist.done: every DOI case shows a due date computed from the department letter date, escalation flags and any written extension.

checklist.step: Put things right for the complainant where the allegation stands
actions: Send the missing disclosure document or Buyer's Guide by tracked mail with a letter naming what was omitted and when it should have been provided.

Where late or missing delivery affected the cancellation decision, reinstate the free-look period from the corrected delivery date, suppress surrender charges and market value adjustment for that window, and confirm it in writing.
Where a surrender charge or market value adjustment was applied inside a period that should have been open, refund it with interest per the state's requirement and record the calculation.
Record on the contract the remedy given, the amount, the date and the approver.
checklist.done: every substantiated case has a tracked corrective mailing and, where relevant, a reinstated free-look and a calculated refund.

checklist.step: Write and clear the response to the department
actions: Draft the response answering each allegation in the department's own order, with the dates, form numbers and edition dates, and attach the acknowledgement image and sent pack image as exhibits.
State plainly where the company was at fault and what has been done, rather than arguing timing on a technicality.
Route to Regulatory Counsel for clearance whenever the response admits a disclosure failure, offers a refund, or touches a systemic defect.
Send inside the department's window, record the send date and method, and attach the sent copy to the case.
checklist.done: a counsel-cleared response is sent inside the window with exhibits attached and the send date recorded.

checklist.step: Assign a root cause that names a system, a document or a person
actions: Pick one root cause from the controlled list: producer did not deliver at application, sale method misclassified, pack component did not resolve, wrong Buyer's Guide edition paired, disclosure edition missing a Section 4C element, free-look parameter wrong for the state, annual report run dropout, returned mail unworked.
Reject 'customer misunderstanding' unless the sent document is confirmed complete, correct for the state and delivered on time.
Name the owning function for the fix: Forms under REG-011-C01, Policy Administration under REG-011-C02, IT under REG-011-C03, or Distribution for producer conduct.
Record the root cause on the case before it can be closed.
checklist.done: every case closes with one controlled root cause and a named owning function.

checklist.step: Size the wider population exposed to the same defect
actions: For each substantiated systemic root cause, query all contracts sharing the defect attribute — same disclosure edition, same state and channel, same product, same release window.
Produce the exposed contract count with issue dates and states and hand it to the Head of Compliance with the complaint file.
Recommend proactive remediation where the exposed count exceeds the agreed threshold, including re-mailing and reinstating free-look periods for contracts that never complained.
Record the decision, the decision maker and the date, whichever way it goes.
checklist.done: every systemic root cause has a quantified exposed contract population and a recorded, owned remediation decision.

checklist.step: Feed producer-attributable complaints into distribution oversight
actions: Aggregate substantiated disclosure complaints by producer National Producer Number and agency on a rolling twelve months.
Verify appointment and licence status in NIPR for the state of solicitation and check the producer's state annuity training credit is current.
Open a conduct review at the second substantiated complaint, requiring pre-issue acknowledgement review for that producer's cases.
Record the action, the review-off criteria and the date on the producer file, and notify the Head of Distribution.
checklist.done: every producer with two or more substantiated complaints has a conduct review with pre-issue controls and a review-off date.

checklist.step: Run the monthly trend review on the disclosure lens
actions: Publish complaint counts by disclosure reason code, state, product, channel and producer for the month and the rolling twelve months.
Compute complaints per thousand contracts in force by state so a small state with a spike is not hidden by volume.
Compare the company's annuity complaint index to the NAIC Consumer Information Source position for the same period and explain any deterioration.
Take every reason code rising two months running to the Compliance Committee with the root causes behind it.
checklist.done: a monthly trend pack exists with per-thousand rates by state and every two-month rising code taken to committee.

checklist.step: Reconcile the register before the Market Conduct Annual Statement
actions: From 1 February, extract the prior calendar year's annuity complaints by state and map each reason code to the MCAS annuity reason taxonomy.
Reconcile the DOI-forwarded subset to the department correspondence log so no complaint the regulator has on file is missing from the submission.
Confirm the state-by-state counts tie to the in-force and new business counts reported on the same MCAS schedule.
Submit by 30 April through the NAIC MCAS application and file the submission confirmation and the final data file as evidence.
checklist.done: the annuity MCAS is reconciled to the complaint register and the DOI log, submitted by 30 April with confirmation filed.

checklist.step: Verify the fix landed before closing the root cause
actions: For each referred root cause, obtain the change or form reference from the owning function and its production date.
Re-test one live case after the fix date — a new issue in the affected state and channel — and confirm the defect no longer occurs.
Keep the complaint root cause open until that re-test passes, regardless of the owning function marking its own ticket done.
Record the re-test date, the evidence and the closer.
checklist.done: every root cause closes only on a dated, evidenced re-test of a live case in the affected state and channel.

checklist.step: Handle free-look cancellation disputes as a distinct queue
actions: Route any complaint about a refused or short-paid free-look cancellation to a dedicated queue with a 5-business-day internal target.
Recompute the free-look expiry from the carrier delivery date and the state parameter for the channel, not from the issue date.
Where the cancellation was inside the recomputed window, process the refund on the state's basis (purchase payments or account value) and pay any required interest.
Report every refused cancellation later found to be inside the window to the Head of Compliance as a breach, not as a service error.
checklist.done: every free-look dispute is recomputed from delivery evidence and any wrongly refused cancellation is refunded and reported.

checklist.step: File the complaint evidence and close
actions: Confirm each closed case holds the complainant correspondence, the delivery evidence pulled, the substantiation conclusion, the DOI response and proof of sending, the remedy record and the root cause.
Apply the three-years-from-closure or next-examination retention label.
Index by complaint id, contract number, state and reason code so an examiner's request by state or by code can be answered directly.
Run a quarterly retrieval check on 20 random closed cases.
checklist.done: every closed case is complete, retention-labelled and retrievable by state, reason code and contract number.

testing.step: Build the complete annuity complaint population for the period
actions: Extract every annuity complaint opened or closed in the period with channel, state, reason codes, receipt date, DOI letter date, response date, disposition and root cause.
Add the department correspondence log and the contact centre annuity disposition report so complaints handled without a case are exposed.
Run a free-text search across contact centre notes and inbound correspondence for disclosure, Buyer's Guide, free look and 'never received' to find uncased complaints.
Reconcile the three sources and treat every uncased complaint as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the population reconciles the case register, the DOI log and the free-text sweep, with uncased complaints listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to the regulator's own view
actions: Match every complaint in the department correspondence log to a case on department file number.
List any department file number with no case, and any case citing a file number the log does not hold.
Compare the state-by-state DOI counts to the counts reported in the annuity MCAS submission for the overlapping year.
Any difference must be explained in writing before sampling, not netted off.
testing.done: every department file number matches a case and the state counts tie to the MCAS submission or are explained.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of DOI-forwarded complaints and 100% of free-look cancellation disputes.
Take 25 further complaints at random with a recorded seed, stratified across disclosure reason codes and states.
Add 10 complaints closed as not substantiated so the not-substantiated call is tested as hard as the substantiated one.
Record the seed, population size and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all DOI and free-look cases and includes not-substantiated closures.

testing.step: Re-perform the reason coding on the sample
actions: Read each sampled complainant letter or call transcript and assign your own disclosure reason code without looking at the recorded one.
Compare and record every difference, particularly complaints coded as service that actually allege non-delivery of the disclosure or Buyer's Guide.
Compute the miscoding rate and compare to the 5% threshold.
Miscoding that would move a complaint out of the MCAS annuity disclosure population is escalated regardless of the overall rate.
testing.done: an independent code exists for each sampled case, with a computed miscoding rate and escalation of MCAS-relevant miscodes.

testing.step: Re-perform the substantiation using the delivery evidence
actions: Pull the notice log rows, acknowledgement image and sent pack image for each sampled contract yourself rather than relying on what the case file holds.
Recompute the delivery timing test for the channel and reach your own substantiated or not-substantiated conclusion.
Compare to the recorded conclusion; a not-substantiated closure with no retrievable acknowledgement is an automatic exception.
Capture the evidence you relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled case has an independent substantiation conclusion built from primary delivery evidence.

testing.step: Recompute every response deadline against the state window
actions: Read the department letter date off the letter image, not the indexed field, for each DOI case.
Look up the state's response window from the department letter and the state complaint-handling rule and recompute the due date.
Compare to the actual response send date and record days early or late for every case.
Confirm any extension claimed has a written department reply on file; an unwritten extension does not stop the clock.
testing.done: every DOI case has a recomputed due date from the letter image and a recorded days-early-or-late figure.

testing.step: Recompute the free-look remedies on the dispute sample
actions: For each free-look dispute, recompute expiry from the carrier delivery date plus the state and channel parameter, applying the 15-day non-face-to-face floor.
Compare the complainant's cancellation request date to the recomputed expiry and decide independently whether the cancellation was in time.
Where in time, recompute the refund on the state's basis (purchase payments or account value) plus any required interest and compare to what was paid.
Any shortfall in refund or any wrongly refused cancellation is a reportable breach with the amount quantified.
testing.done: every dispute has an independent in-time decision and a recomputed refund amount compared to what was paid.

testing.step: Trace root causes through to a verified production fix
actions: For each sampled systemic root cause, obtain the referral to Forms, Policy Administration or IT and the change or form reference.
Confirm the fix reached production, read its production date and confirm the post-fix re-test evidence exists.
Confirm the exposed contract population was quantified and that a recorded, signed decision exists on proactive remediation.
A root cause closed with no re-test, or with an unquantified exposed population, is an exception.
testing.done: every sampled systemic root cause traces to a production fix, a dated re-test and a signed population decision.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with the complaint id, contract number, state, the failing element and any consumer detriment amount.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: complaint not cased, miscoded, evidence not pulled, deadline computed from the wrong date, substantiation wrong, remedy short paid, population not sized.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel where a DOI response understated a failure.
Carry every open issue into the next monthly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a detriment amount where applicable, a root cause, an owner, a date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the complaint test
actions: Compute the on-time DOI response rate, the miscoding rate and the substantiation agreement rate against their thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — separating consumer detriment findings from process findings.
Have the independent reviewer, who handled and closed none of the sampled complaints, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee with the trend pack and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, the three rates and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual independent audit of annuity disclosure content and delivery timing; the audit is performed by Internal Audit with no involvement from Compliance, Forms or Policy Administration

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the audit programme is written directly from Model 245 Section 4B delivery timing, Section 4C disclosure contents, Section 5 annual report and the record retention rule, with the state variation testing anchored on the Alaska adoption of NAIC Model 245 and extended to the Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona adoptions

In-scope processes.value: The full annuity disclosure chain end to end — forms authoring (C01), delivery and notice logging (C02), system configuration (C03), training (C04) and complaint handling (C05) — for group and individual deferred annuity contracts issued in all 45 adopting jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: Audit programme, sampling record, workpapers, issue register and the management action tracker, with read-only extracts drawn from the Policy Administration Platform and the form inventory

Compliance procedure documented.value: Annuity Disclosure Audit Programme — population build from the admin system rather than the notice log, stratified sampling by state and channel, element-by-element Section 4C re-performance, timing recomputation, and the issue rating and closure standard

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Audit Executive and noted by the Audit Committee in the annual plan; the programme is refreshed each year against the current Model 245 text and the prior year's market conduct examination findings

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual — fieldwork completed and the draft report issued within 30 days of fieldwork close, management responses within 15 business days, final report to the Audit Committee at its next scheduled meeting, and all high-rated actions closed within 90 days

Deadline reminders configured.value: Audit milestone alerts at planning, fieldwork close, draft issue, response due and report issue; the action tracker sends 30, 14 and 7 day alerts before each agreed action date and escalates overdue high-rated actions to the Chief Audit Executive weekly

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Audit programme, population extracts, sampling record, workpapers with captured screens, issue register and management responses retained seven years under the audit records policy, exceeding the Model 245 three-year minimum

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every audit finding is raised as a rated issue with the affected contract count, the responsible function, an agreed management action, an owner and a due date, tracked to evidenced closure

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs the final report and approves closure of every high-rated issue only on re-performed evidence, never on management assertion

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All annuity contracts issued in the audit year plus all contract anniversaries triggering a Section 5 annual report, drawn from the policy administration system independently of the compliance notice log, across all 45 jurisdictions

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on a face-to-face contract with no acknowledgement or an acknowledgement dated after the application, on a pack issued without the Buyer's Guide, and on a free-look period below the state minimum; a single occurrence drives a high-rated issue and a population impact assessment

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The underlying obligation is per sale and per anniversary; the independent audit is annual with a mid-year follow-up limited to retesting prior-year high-rated issues

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer is outside the first and second lines entirely; the audit team must include no one who worked in Compliance, Forms or Policy Administration during the audit year

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual annuity disclosure audit file in AuditBoard — programme, population extracts with row counts, sampling record with seed, per-sample workpapers with captured screens, issue register and management responses

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Final audit report with scope, population, sample basis, findings by Model 245 section, ratings and management actions, releasable to a market conduct examiner or a state examination team on request within 5 business days

checklist.step: Plan the audit against the current Model 245 text and prior findings
actions: Re-read Model 245 Sections 4B, 4C and 5 and the record retention rule, and pull the current state variation grid from Compliance without adopting it as fact.
Read last year's audit issues, the market conduct examination findings and the substantiated disclosure complaints from REG-011-C05 to target the scope.
Write the audit programme with one test step per Model 245 requirement and a stated evidence source for each.
Get the programme approved by the Chief Audit Executive and issue the engagement letter to the Head of Compliance and the Policy Admin Ops Lead naming the fieldwork dates.
checklist.done: an approved programme exists with a test step per Model 245 requirement and an issued engagement letter.

checklist.step: Build the population from the admin system, not from the compliance log
actions: Extract every annuity contract issued in the audit year with contract number, product, writing company, state of solicitation, sale method, application signature date, issue date, contract delivery date and producer National Producer Number.
Extract every contract anniversary in the year for the Section 5 annual report population.
Take the extract through a read-only account so the population cannot be filtered by the audited function.
Record the extract query, the run timestamp and the row counts in the workpaper.
checklist.done: both populations are extracted read-only with the query, timestamp and row counts recorded.

checklist.step: Reconcile the population to independent counts before testing
actions: Reconcile the issued-contract count to the finance new business production report and the statutory annuity considerations for the year.
Reconcile the anniversary count to the in-force listing at each month end.
Investigate and document every difference above 0.5% before any sample is drawn.
Have the extractor sign the population as complete.
checklist.done: both populations reconcile to independent counts within tolerance and are signed as complete.

checklist.step: Stratify and draw a reproducible sample
actions: Stratify by sale method and by state group, giving mandatory coverage to Alaska, Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona plus the ten highest-volume states.
Take at least 25 contracts per sale method stratum with volume, 100% of contracts issued in the first 30 days after any disclosure edition change, and 15 group annuity certificate deliveries.
Take 30 anniversaries for the Section 5 test, selected at random with a recorded seed.
Record the seed, stratum sizes, selection date and the reason for each mandatory stratum so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
checklist.done: the sample is stratified, includes the mandated states and edition-change window, and is reproducible from the recorded seed.

checklist.step: Re-perform the Section 4C content test on the editions actually sent
actions: For each sampled contract, retrieve the exact sent PDF image rather than the current template.

Tick off each Section 4C element against your own list — long-term-nature statement, guaranteed and non-guaranteed elements with limitations, crediting method, surrender and withdrawal charges and their period, market value adjustment, all fees and rider charges, annuitization options, the 10% early-distribution tax penalty and the questions contact — recording page and paragraph.
Compare the surrender charge schedule printed to the contract's own data pages so a stale table is caught.
Capture every defect as a screenshot into the workpaper with the contract number stamped on it.
checklist.done: every sampled sent image has an element-by-element grid with page references and captured defects.

checklist.step: Recompute delivery timing for every sampled contract
actions: For face-to-face sales, read the acknowledgement receipt date and the application signature date off the images and compute the difference in days.
For mail, telephone and internet sales, read the carrier delivery date or DocuSign completion timestamp and compare it to the contract delivery date recorded.
Confirm the disclosure and Buyer's Guide were in the same package as the contract for non-face-to-face sales, not sent afterwards.
Record a pass or fail per contract with the day count, never a narrative conclusion.
checklist.done: every sampled contract carries a recomputed day count and a binary pass or fail on Section 4B timing.

checklist.step: Re-verify the Buyer's Guide edition and the state variable text
actions: Read the Buyer's Guide title and edition from the sent image and compare it to the NAIC current edition for that product type as at the issue date.
Confirm any state-published guide required in the sampled state was used instead of the NAIC guide where applicable.
Read the free-look days and refund basis printed on the notice and compare them to the state's adopting text read independently, not to the company's variation grid.
Treat a shorter-than-statutory printed free-look as a high-rated finding with the exposed contract count.
checklist.done: every sampled contract's Buyer's Guide edition and printed free-look terms are verified against primary sources.

checklist.step: Test the Section 5 annual report sample for timing, completeness and accuracy
actions: Retrieve the sent annual report image for each sampled anniversary and compute days from anniversary date to send date against the 30-day standard.
Confirm every Section 5 field is present: beginning and end of period contract value, gross purchase payments, interest credited, charges deducted, withdrawals, surrender value and death benefit.
Tie the end-of-period contract value and the interest credited to the policy administration values at the anniversary date to the cent.
List any sampled anniversary with no report at all as a high-rated finding.
checklist.done: each sampled anniversary has a day count, a field-completeness check and a value tie to the admin record.

checklist.step: Test the retention rule on the evidence itself
actions: For 25 sampled contracts, attempt to retrieve the acknowledgement image, the sent pack image and the tracking reference within the repository and time each retrieval.
Confirm the retention label applied is three years from contract termination or the next examination, whichever is later, and that nothing in the sample is due to purge early.
Test five contracts terminated more than three years ago to confirm records were retained through the last examination rather than purged on the calendar rule.
Record any unretrievable artefact as an evidence failure independent of whether the underlying delivery occurred.
checklist.done: retrieval is demonstrated and timed for 25 contracts and the retention labelling is verified including terminated contracts.

checklist.step: Test the controls behind the results, not just the outcomes
actions: Attempt to issue a face-to-face test case with no acknowledgement and confirm the system blocks rather than warns, capturing the screen.
Re-perform the parameter table to variation grid reconciliation for ten states yourself, using the state adopting texts as the anchor.
Test that the training completion register covers everyone who processed a sampled contract, and check their completion status at the processing date.
Test that complaints alleging non-delivery on any sampled contract were cased, coded and substantiated correctly.
checklist.done: the acknowledgement gate, parameter reconciliation, training currency and complaint handling are each independently re-performed.

checklist.step: Quantify every finding in contracts and consumer impact
actions: For each finding, project the sample error rate onto its stratum and state the estimated affected contract count with the projection method.
For free-look and surrender charge findings, compute the monetary exposure using the charges actually applied within the disputed window.
Separate confirmed occurrences from projected occurrences so management cannot argue the projection to dismiss the confirmed cases.
Have a second auditor recompute the projection before it goes into the draft report.
checklist.done: every finding carries a confirmed count, a projected count with method, and a monetary exposure where applicable.

checklist.step: Raise, rate and agree the issues with management
actions: Raise one issue per root cause, not per instance, citing the Model 245 section breached and the workpaper references.
Rate high any missing Buyer's Guide, post-application acknowledgement, short free-look or missing annual report; rate medium documentation and retrieval failures.
Hold the closing meeting with the Head of Compliance, the Policy Admin Ops Lead, the Head of IT and the Learning Development Manager and agree an action, owner and date per issue.
Refuse actions that only add monitoring where the defect is a system rule or a document content gap.
checklist.done: every issue has a rating, a Model 245 citation, an agreed action with a named owner and a date, recorded in the tracker.

checklist.step: Issue the report and take it to the Audit Committee
actions: Issue the draft within 30 days of fieldwork close and collect management responses within 15 business days.
State an overall opinion on the annuity disclosure control environment with the population, sample basis and error rates on the face of the report.
Present the final report to the Audit Committee at its next meeting, naming any high-rated issue and any consumer remediation required.
Notify the Head of Compliance where a finding is likely to require a regulator self-report so Regulatory Counsel can assess it in parallel.
checklist.done: a signed final report with an overall opinion is issued and presented, with self-report candidates referred to Counsel.

checklist.step: Track actions to evidenced closure
actions: Send 30, 14 and 7 day alerts before each agreed action date and escalate overdue high-rated actions to the Chief Audit Executive weekly.
Require closure evidence of the kind the action promised: a production configuration extract, a filed form edition, a completion register, not a status update.
Re-test one live case per closed high-rated action — a contract issued after the fix in the affected state and channel.
Refuse closure where the re-test fails and reset the action date with the owner.
checklist.done: no high-rated action closes without a passing re-test on a live post-fix case.

checklist.step: File the audit file and feed next year's plan
actions: Complete the audit file: programme, population extracts and reconciliations, sampling record with seed, per-sample workpapers with captured screens, issue register and management responses.
Apply the seven-year audit retention and index by audit year, Model 245 section and state.
Write the carry-forward note listing which states, products and channels were not covered this year so next year's stratification closes the gap.
Hand the substantiated systemic findings to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for the examination readiness pack.
checklist.done: the audit file is complete, retention-labelled, indexed, and a carry-forward coverage note exists for next year's plan.

testing.step: Verify the audit population was built independently and completely
actions: Re-run the population query from the read-only account and compare row counts to the counts recorded in the audit file.
Confirm the extract came from the policy administration system rather than the compliance notice log, since a log-based population cannot find an unlogged contract.
Check the anniversary population against the in-force listing at each month end independently of the audit team's reconciliation.
Any count difference over 0.5% unexplained in the file is a quality failure on the audit itself.
testing.done: the population is re-run, matched to the recorded counts and confirmed to originate from the admin system.

testing.step: Reconcile the sample back to the population and the stated method
actions: Re-draw the sample using the recorded seed and stratum sizes and compare item for item to the sample tested.
Confirm the mandatory strata were actually taken: Alaska, Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona, the ten highest-volume states, the post-edition-change window and the group annuity certificates.
List any tested item not in the re-drawn sample, which indicates the sample was altered after selection.
Confirm every sample item has a completed workpaper — a drawn but untested item is an exception.
testing.done: the sample re-draws identically, the mandatory strata are present and every drawn item has a workpaper.

testing.step: Re-perform a sub-sample of the Section 4C content conclusions
actions: Take 15 workpapers concluded as compliant and open the sent PDF images yourself.

Run the Section 4C element list independently and compare to the auditor's grid, paying particular attention to market value adjustment, rider charges and the tax penalty statement which are the elements most often missed.
Record any element the auditor passed that you fail, with the page reference.
A disagreement rate above 10% means the content test itself is unreliable and the audit conclusion must be qualified.
testing.done: 15 compliant conclusions are independently re-performed with a computed disagreement rate.

testing.step: Recompute the timing maths on a sub-sample
actions: Take 20 sampled contracts across all four sale methods and recompute the acknowledgement-to-application day difference and the delivery-date comparison from the source images.
Recompute the free-look expiry from the delivery evidence and the state's adopting text read directly, not from the variation grid.
Compare to the auditor's recorded pass or fail and list every difference.
Any contract the audit passed that this recomputation fails is escalated to the Chief Audit Executive immediately.
testing.done: 20 contracts have independently recomputed timing and free-look results compared to the audit conclusions.

testing.step: Test that findings were quantified correctly
actions: Re-run the projection for each finding using the recorded sample error rate and stratum size and compare to the reported affected contract count.
Recompute the monetary exposure on free-look and surrender charge findings from the charges actually applied inside the disputed windows.
Confirm confirmed occurrences and projected occurrences are reported separately in the final report.
Any understated count or exposure is a reportable quality failure.
testing.done: every finding's projection and monetary exposure is independently recomputed and matched to the report.

testing.step: Test issue ratings against the stated rating standard
actions: List every issue with its rating and check it against the programme's rating rules — missing Buyer's Guide, post-application acknowledgement, short free-look and missing annual report are high by definition.
Flag any high-qualifying finding rated medium or low and read the rationale recorded for the downgrade.
Confirm each issue is raised per root cause rather than per instance, so a single systemic defect is not fragmented into low-rated pieces.
Escalate any pattern of downgrading to the Audit Committee chair.
testing.done: every rating is checked against the rating rules and every downgrade has a recorded, reviewed rationale.

testing.step: Test management actions for substance and closure evidence
actions: Take every high-rated issue closed in the period and read the closure evidence attached.
Confirm the evidence is of the promised kind — production configuration extract, filed form edition, completion register — and not a management status update.
Confirm the post-fix re-test was performed on a live contract issued after the fix date in the affected state and channel, and read its result.
Any high-rated issue closed without that re-test is reopened.
testing.done: every closed high-rated issue holds promised-kind evidence and a passing live post-fix re-test, or is reopened.

testing.step: Test auditor independence and coverage
actions: Check the HRIS history of every team member for any role in Compliance, Forms, Policy Administration or IT during the audit year.
Confirm no team member tested work they previously performed and that the reviewer of each workpaper is not its preparer.
Read the carry-forward coverage note and confirm the states, products and channels omitted this year are scheduled into next year's plan.
Record an independence confirmation on the audit file signed by each team member.
testing.done: independence is confirmed for every team member and the coverage gap is scheduled into the next plan.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per audit-quality exception with the workpaper reference, what was missed and the effect on the audit conclusion.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: population sourced from the log, sample altered after selection, element test incomplete, timing recomputed from indexed fields, finding under-quantified, rating downgraded, closure evidence insufficient.
Set an owner in Internal Audit and a remediation date, and where the audit conclusion is affected reissue the report rather than amending it quietly.
Carry every open issue into the mid-year follow-up as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every audit-quality exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report on the audit's reliability
actions: Compute the re-performance disagreement rate, the rating-downgrade count and the closure-evidence failure count against their thresholds.
Write the conclusion — the audit is reliable, reliable with qualifications, or must be re-performed — with the workpaper references behind each judgement.
Have the independent reviewer, who performed no fieldwork on this audit, sign the quality workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee alongside the annuity disclosure audit report and file both in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed quality workpaper with a stated reliability conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.
